dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5801.text: Ghost-related customs. Formed from 鬼, with 幾 indicating the sound. The Huainan Commentary says: “The people of Wu are 鬼; the people of Yue, 𩴪.” The distinction in this quotation is uncertain.

shuowen:5802.text: The sound of ghosts and spirits, 䰰䰰 without stopping. Formed from 鬼, with 需 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5803.text: A ghost’s transformation. Formed from 鬼, with 化 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5804.text: An exclamation on being startled by a ghost. Formed from 鬼, with abbreviated 難 indicating the sound. Read like 儺 in the Odes’ “Receive blessings without weariness.”

shuowen:5805.text: A ghost’s appearance. Formed from 鬼, with 賓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5806.text: Hateful. Formed from 鬼, with 酉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5807.text: A divine beast. Formed from 鬼, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5808.text: A kind of ghost. Formed from 鬼 and 离; 离 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5809.text: A ghost. Formed from 鬼, with 麻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5810.text: Fright in a dream. Formed from 鬼, with 厭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5811.text: A ghost’s head. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 甶.

shuowen:5812.text: Aversion or fear. Formed from 甶 and abbreviated 虎: a ghost’s head and tiger’s claws are fearful.

shuowen:5813.text: A kind of monkey, its head resembling a ghost’s. Formed from 甶 and 禸.

shuowen:5814.text: Wicked and crooked. Han Fei says: “When Cangjie made characters, acting for oneself was 厶.” All characters in this group follow 厶.

shuowen:5815.text: Taking by force against rightful order is 篡. Formed from 厶, with 算 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5816.text: To entice and call to one another. Formed from 厶 and 羑.

shuowen:5817.text: High and uneven. Formed from 山, with 鬼 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 嵬.

shuowen:5818.text: High. Formed from 嵬, with 委 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5819.text: To spread: spreading qi, dispersing it and producing all things; stony and high. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 山.

shuowen:5820.text: The sacred peaks: east, 岱; south, 靃; west, 華; north, 恆; center, 泰室. These are where the king arrives on inspection tours. Formed from 山, with 獄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5821.text: Mount Tai. Formed from 山, with 代 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5822.text: Mountains occurring in the sea where one may stop and rest are 㠀. Formed from 山, with 鳥 indicating the sound. Read like 蔦 in the Odes’ “Dodder and lichen.”

shuowen:5823.text: A mountain in Qi territory. Formed from 山, with 狃 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “You met me among the hills of Nao.”

shuowen:5824.text: Mount Geyi in Xiapi, Donghai. Formed from 山, with 睪 indicating the sound. The Book of Xia says: “The solitary paulownias on Yi’s sunny slopes.”

shuowen:5825.text: Mount Fengyu between Wu and Chu, in the state of Wangmang. Formed from 山, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5826.text: Mount Jiuyi, where Shun is buried, in Yingdao, Lingling. Formed from 山, with 疑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5827.text: A mountain beyond the western frontier of Jiandi, Shu. Formed from 山, with 𢽹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5828.text: A mountain. Some say it is the source of the Weak River. Formed from 山, with 几 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5829.text: Mount 巀𡾦 in Chiyang, Pingyi. Formed from 山, with 𢧵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5830.text: Mount 巀𡾦. Formed from 山, with 辥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5831.text: A mountain in Huayin, Hongnong. Formed from 山, with abbreviated 華 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5832.text: A mountain in Yanmen. Formed from 山, with 𩫖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5833.text: Mount Yang in Liaoxi. Formed from 山, with 昜 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 嵎鐵崵谷, a valley location whose precise wording is uncertain.

shuowen:5834.text: A mountain with vegetation. Formed from 山, with 古 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Climb that wooded hill.”

shuowen:5835.text: A mountain without vegetation. Formed from 山, with 己 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Climb that bare hill.”

shuowen:5836.text: A mountain with many large stones. Formed from 山, with abbreviated 學 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5837.text: A mountain with many small stones. Formed from 山, with 敖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5838.text: Rock bearing earth on top. Formed from 山, with 且 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Climb that rocky hill.”

shuowen:5839.text: A mountain’s backbone. Formed from 山, with 网 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5840.text: A small but high mountain. Formed from 山, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5841.text: A mountain rising high, 岑崟. Formed from 山, with 金 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5842.text: Precipitous and high. Formed from 山, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5843.text: A small, pointed mountain. Formed from 山, with 䜌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5844.text: A mountain resembling a hall. Formed from 山, with 宓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5845.text: A mountain cave. Formed from 山, with 由 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5846.text: High. Formed from 山, with 陖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5847.text: Mountains lying low, 墮墮; the precise appearance is uncertain. Formed from 山, with abbreviated 憜 indicating the sound. Read like 憜 in pushing one another down.

shuowen:5848.text: Exceptionally high. Formed from 山, with 棧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5849.text: A short, high mountain. Formed from 山, with 屈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5850.text: Lofty and high. Formed from 山, with 蠆 indicating the sound. Read like 厲.

shuowen:5851.text: A mountain’s summit. Formed from 山, with 夆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5852.text: A cliff. Formed from 山, with 嚴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5853.text: A mountain crag. Formed from 山 and 品. Read like 吟.

shuowen:5854.text: A mountain appearance, 𡽕. Formed from 山, with 絫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5855.text: A mountain’s appearance. Formed from 山, with 辠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5856.text: A mountain’s appearance. Another explanation: a mountain name. Formed from 山, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5857.text: A mountain’s appearance. Formed from 山, with 隓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5858.text: A mountain’s appearance. Formed from 山, with 𢀩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5859.text: Towering, 嵯峨. Formed from 山, with 我 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5860.text: Towering, 嶸. Formed from 山, with 青 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5861.text: Towering, 崝嶸. Formed from 山, with 榮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5862.text: A valley. Formed from 山, with 坙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5863.text: A mountain collapsing. Formed from 山, with 朋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5864.text: A road along a mountain’s side. Formed from 山, with 弗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5865.text: A mountain name. Formed from 山, with 敄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5866.text: 焦嶢, the appearance of a high mountain. Formed from 山, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5867.text: A mountain high, 𡺲. Formed from 山, with 戕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5868.text: Mount Jiuzong in Gukou, Pingyi. Formed from 山, with 㚇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5869.text: A corner or recess, a joint of a high mountain. Formed from 山 and 卪.

shuowen:5870.text: Lofty and high. Formed from 山, with 宗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5871.text: Great and high. Formed from 山, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5872.text: 嶙峋, the appearance of deep cliffs. Formed from 山, with 粦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5873.text: The cliff appearance 嶙峋. Formed from 山, with 旬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5874.text: A mountain’s high appearance. Formed from 山, with 及 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5875.text: A pointed, high mountain. Formed from 山, with 喬 indicating the sound. Ancient writing also uses 喬.

shuowen:5876.text: A mountain’s deep appearance. Formed from 山, with abbreviated 歁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5877.text: An island. Formed from 山, with 與 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5878.text: A mountain road. Formed from 山, with 領 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5879.text: A mountain name. Formed from 山, with abbreviated 葻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5880.text: The central sacred peak, Mount Songgao. Formed from 山 and 高; some forms use 松. Wei Zhao’s commentary on the Discourses of the States says: “Ancient writing also uses 崇.”

shuowen:5881.text: Kunlun, a mountain name. Formed from 山, with 昆 indicating the sound. Yang Xiong’s writings in the Book of Han also use 昆侖.

shuowen:5882.text: The mountain 崑崙. Formed from 山, with 侖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5883.text: A mountain name. Formed from 山, with abbreviated 稽 indicating the sound. The Xi clan specially invented this graph when fleeing danger; it is not ancient.

shuowen:5884.text: Two mountains. All characters in this group follow 屾.

shuowen:5885.text: A mountain in Kuaiji. Another explanation: Dangtu, 當嵞, in Jiujiang. People marry on xin, ren, gui and jia days. Formed from 屾, with 余 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “I married at Mount Tu.”

shuowen:5886.text: A high bank. Formed from 山 and 厂; 厂 also indicates the sound. All characters in this group follow 屵.

shuowen:5887.text: A high waterside cliff. Formed from 屵, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5888.text: A high edge. Formed from 屵, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5889.text: High. Formed from 屵, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5890.text: To collapse. Formed from 屵, with 肥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5891.text: The sound of collapse. Formed from 屵, with 配 indicating the sound. Read like 費.

shuowen:5892.text: Making a dwelling against a shelter, depicting a tall building facing and projecting outward; the graphical wording is uncertain. All characters in this group follow 广. Read like 儼 in 儼然.

shuowen:5893.text: A store for documents. Formed from 广, with 付 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5894.text: The Son of Heaven’s Biyong hall for ceremonial feasting. Formed from 广, with 雝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5895.text: Where ritual officials care for the aged. Xia called it 校, Yin 庠, Zhou 序. Formed from 广, with 羊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5896.text: A temporary dwelling, left in autumn and winter and inhabited in spring and summer. Formed from 广, with 盧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5897.text: The interior of a palace. Formed from 广, with 廷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5898.text: A central courtyard. Formed from 广, with 畱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5899.text: The wall of a multistory building. Formed from 广, with 屯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5900.text: A covered gallery. Formed from 广, with 牙 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “In summer shelter the horses in a gallery.”
